input.quote: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
input.rationale: Section 14.3 selects New York substantive law, which is our preferred governing law, and there is no arbitration provision (no hits for "arbitration") and no venue or forum clause anywhere in the agreement (no hits for "venue"; jurisdiction references are only generic "court of competent jurisdiction" in §§ 8.2 and 14.5). The rule's preferred position requires both New York law and exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, so the missing forum element is a deviation. Minimal fix: append exclusive New York County venue language to § 14.3, leaving the existing choice-of-law sentence intact.

ops.oldText: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
ops.newText: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions. The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any dispute arising out of or related to this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] New York law already matches our position, so we have only added exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York County to remove any doubt about forum. This keeps disputes in a single accepted court and avoids litigation in an unspecified or foreign venue.
proposal.summary: Add exclusive New York County court venue to the New York choice-of-law clause.
